newsitem.title: USA: Russia interested in 'variety' of US ag goods.
newsitem.headline: Russia interested in 'variety' of US ag goods.

text.p: Russia is interested in buying a variety of U.S. agricultural goods, ranging from wheat and wheat products to soybeans and cotton, Agriculture Department's General Sales Manager said Tuesday.

Chris Goldthwait said that in recent talks in Washington between U.S. and Russian officials during the Gore-Chernomyrdin commission meetings, Russian officials said they were interested in purchasing a range of U.S. products this year.
"Russian business could spread across a number of commodities," Goldthwait told Reuters. "There were a number of products mentioned."

Goldthwait said he was puzzled about a published report on Tuesday from Moscow that an agreement was reached during last month's meetings for Russian to purchase 25,000 to 30,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans in the first half of this year with U.S. export credits.

"There was not any formal agreement on any transactions," he said. "We have private GSM 102 (credit) under which soybeans are an eligible product...but there was no specific agreement on a specific transaction."
Goldthwait, however, said he would not be surprised if Russia would be in the market for U.S. soybeans, and said that annual Russian demand for U.S. soybeans could be as high as 300,000 tonnes.
He said purchases would likely be made in fairly small-size lots, probably in the 25,000 to 30,000 tonne range.
USDA last week raised Russia's GSM-102 credit guarantee line by $20 million to $70 million for fiscal yar 1997.
Goldthwait said Monday that USDA is considering providing supplier creidt guarantees on U.S. ag exports to Russia, but has reached no decision.
